mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 3.0% signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 3.0% but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month sequential increase in unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month moving averages signal a broad-based demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: RSAFS and HOUST both decline below 12-month MA but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) triggers equity market underperformance as real rates rise and corporate margins compress, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production index above 105 (2017=100) indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO above 105 but 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment growth below 50,000 jobs per month signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth < 50,000 but 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 6-month averages indicate a severe demand shock that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS and HOUST both decline below 6-month MA but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high-growth economic regimes (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3.0%), rising consumer spending (RSAFS) combined with expanding housing starts (HOUST) signals robust demand that drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 > 3% q/q with RSAFS and HOUST rising but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
